text:
Mark Stone became the Golden Knights' all-time points leader this month. He tied the franchise record with a power-play goal against Vancouver on Nov. 15, then took it outright four nights later by setting up Victor Olofsson against Dallas, his 418th point, as Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted. It came in a rough week: the Canucks game was a 6-3 loss, and asked whether Vegas overlooked the opponent, Stone told Granger, "The result for sure shows that."

At 34, the captain has 11 goals and 23 points in 25 games, 13 on the power play. The goals are generous (25.6% shooting against a talent range near 17.3%), and Vegas has scored 5.8 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which pads the points. The last ten games were quiet: six points against 10.4 expected, and his team is under 50% of the 5v5 attempts with him out there.

His record argues against reading much into one slow month. Evolving-Hockey ranked him third among 401 forwards last season at 4.1 wins above replacement, built at both ends: opponents got 0.17 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice.
